title: What composing like cycles is good for: codes, constraint complexity and counting
claim: (1) Codes. If the law of a relation composes like cycles, every matroid of its systems is a direct sum of rank-one parallel classes and matroids representable over finite fields; with trivial tops, full coordinate ranges and a circuit of three or more variables, the relation is a coset of a module code over a finite field. So the Simonis-Ashikhmin almost affine code over F_3^2, whose matroid is the non-Pappus matroid, generates a law that fails elimination: an equivalence of the alphabet defined by one copy, attached to two coordinates of another, gives a three-copy system with circuits {c1,w1} and {c1,c4,c5,w2} whose union without c1 is free. (2) Complexity. If a single-sorted law with all constants added composes like cycles, its polymorphism algebra is Taylor (no two-element projection algebra lies in HS), so by the CSP dichotomy theorem its constraint problem is in P; with trivial tops a genuine Mal'tsev polymorphism exists. One-in-three, not-all-equal and 3-colouring each fail elimination. (3) Counting. The lifted Z3 law and K4 compose like cycles but are not balanced, so counting their solutions is #P-complete. (4) Constants can destroy composing like cycles: parity beside J and K4 each have a system with one constant that fails elimination, so the hypothesis of (2) is strictly stronger than composing like cycles, and whether every law composing like cycles has a polynomial-time constraint problem is open.
failure_conditions: A law composing like cycles has a system whose matroid has a component of rank two or more representable over no finite field.
The rebuilt code is not almost affine, its matroid is not non-Pappus, or the exhibited system satisfies elimination.
A single-sorted law that composes like cycles with all constants added has a non-Taylor polymorphism algebra.
The lifted Z3 law or K4 is balanced.
One of the exhibited systems with a constant satisfies elimination.
foundation_claim_scope: Consequences of the composition characterization for codes, constraint complexity and counting. No native recurrence, composed topology in the protected sense, path, metric distance or physical claim, and no claim about P versus NP.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py rebuilds the non-Pappus code (729 codewords, almost affine, the eight lines), its three unary polymorphisms, the one-copy line equivalence and the three-copy failing system; the hardness systems; x - y + z with constants for Z3, parity and the GF(4) law; the counting matrices; the two systems with constants and 750 sampled systems; five controls rejected; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with explicit and randomized checks; AFFINE-TOPS-20261021-001A-P001 and B-P001, the Taylor criterion for finite idempotent algebras, the CSP dichotomy theorem (Bulatov; Zhuk), the counting dichotomy (Dyer and Richerby) and Pappus's theorem are cited; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: candidate-local-delta: corollaries of AFFINE-TOPS-20261021-001A-P001 and B-P001 with classical theorems (Pappus, the Taylor criterion, the CSP dichotomy, the counting dichotomy); the explicit systems and the refutation that constants preserve composing like cycles are new to the program; novelty scan no-overlap-in-bounded-search for the characterization itself.
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-21.
